newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Bids for British drugstore chain move closer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bids for British drugstore chain move closer.

text.p: Renewed takeover bids for Lloyds Chemists Plc may be only days away after news on Tuesday that the British drugstore chain had received numerous offers from prospective purchasers of some of its wholesale businesses.
"I am not suprised by this. We were being lined up for a renewal of bidding, maybe as early as this week," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
The company said the sales of the wholesaling units would only take place if either UniChem Plc or Gehe AG were successful in acquiring Lloyds Chemists.
"The Board has been particularly encouraged by the number of parties who have responded and the values which they have attributed to the businesses in question," the company said in a statement.
Lloyds said it has forwarded signed heads of terms to Unichem and Gehe to assist them in satisfying conditions laid down by Britain's Secretary of State for Trade and Industry.

Gehe's 620 million pound ($966.5 million) bid for Lloyds lapsed in March along with a similar bid by rival UniChem after the British government referred them to the UK's Monopolies and Merger's Commission.
Last month the British government said bids by either UniChem or Gehe could go ahead if certain assets were sold off.

Gehe has been in talks over the past fortnight with potential buyers of Lloyds' wholesale division and has said it would make a new bid for Britain's second largest drugstore chain once it had met the British government's requirements.

Analysts believe UniChem has been engaged in similar discussions, noting that both of Lloyds' suitors have to find buyers for the wholesale businesses by the British government's deadline of October 18.

"There really isn't anything new in the Lloyds statement. The market knows the wholesale business will have buyers by October 18," another analyst said. "But, it does bring the process one-step closer," he added.
Analysts expect fresh bids for Lloyds to surface in the next few weeks but Lloyds' profits warning last month combined with the asset disposals may prompt a modest mark down in the final offer price.

"Clearly, demands that we find buyers for some Lloyds assets, and the profit warning changes the value of Lloyds, but we have not yet decided how these factors may influence a future bid we may make," Gehe's chief financial officer Karl-Gerhard Eick told Reuters earlier this month.
Such comments have led analysts to expect Gehe to bid something less than its original 500 pence per share cash offer.

The prize in the upcoming bidding contest will be supremacy in Britain's retail pharmaceutical market. UniChem and Gehe both already have around a third of the British drug retailing market, while Lloyds' share is about five percent.

Analysts said the industrial logic of the acquisition is strong for both firms. UniChem is trying to dominatate its home market, while Gehe wants to expand after entering the British market last year by buying drugs distributor AAH Plc.
Lloyds Chemists shares were up six pence to 497p by midday.
